title: All Entities are Not Created Equal: Examining the Long Tail for Ultra-Fine Entity Typing
abstract: arXiv:2410.17355v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Due to their capacity to acquire world knowledge from large corpora, pre-trained language models (PLMs) are extensively used in ultra-fine entity typing tasks where the space of labels is extremely large. In this work, we explore the limitations of the knowledge acquired by PLMs by proposing a novel heuristic to approximate the pre-training distribution of entities when the pre-training data is unknown. Then, we systematically demonstrate that entity-typing approaches that rely solely on the parametric knowledge of PLMs struggle significantly with entities at the long tail of the pre-training distribution, and that knowledge-infused approaches can account for some of these shortcomings. Our findings suggest that we need to go beyond PLMs to produce solutions that perform well for infrequent entities.

translated_title: 并非所有实体生而平等：研究超细粒度实体类型分类中的长尾问题
translated_abstract: 由于预训练语言模型（PLMs）具有从大型语料库中获取世界知识的能力，它们被广泛应用于标签空间极其庞大的超细粒度实体类型分类任务中。在这项工作中，我们通过提出一种新颖的启发式方法来近似实体的预训练分布（在预训练数据未知的情况下），从而探索预训练语言模型所获取知识的局限性。随后，我们系统地证明了仅依赖预训练语言模型参数化知识的实体类型分类方法在处理处于预训练分布长尾的实体时表现显著不佳，而知识注入方法可以部分弥补这些不足。我们的研究结果表明，我们需要超越预训练语言模型，才能为不常见实体提供表现良好的解决方案。
tldr: 本研究提出一种新颖的启发式方法来近似实体的预训练分布，系统揭示了仅依赖预训练语言模型参数化知识的实体类型分类方法在处理长尾实体时表现显著不佳，表明需要超越预训练语言模型的方法来应对不常见实体。
en_tdlr: This work proposes a novel heuristic to approximate entity pre-training distributions and systematically demonstrates that PLM-based ultra-fine entity typing methods struggle significantly with long-tail entities, suggesting that solutions beyond PLMs' parametric knowledge are needed for infrequent entities.
